key_insight: A weakly supervised PET representation-learning approach that uses H&E-derived guidance during training can better retrieve intra-tumour heterogeneity than PET-only global embeddings.
clinical_relevance: This could help future PET-based tools more accurately identify biologically meaningful tumour subregions without requiring histopathology at inference time.
method: Teacher-student framework learns PET voxel representations from pathology-informed supervision.
Generates both global and hotspot-conditioned embeddings plus heterogeneity maps.
Uses progressive ablations to isolate the contribution of each supervision component.
evidence_signal: Across cross-validation, hotspot-conditioned PET representations improved retrieval metrics such as mAP, nDCG, and MRR versus global PET and conventional baselines, with additional perturbation/deletion and histology-concordance analyses.
watch_item: Results come from a specific oesophageal cancer test case, so broader generalisability and clinical deployment robustness still need validation.
paper_title: Weakly Supervised Pathology-Informed Representation Learning for PET-Based Content Retrieval of Intra-Tumour Heterogeneity
